query: Find approximately five independent primary empirical or evaluation papers for GPTScan and SAILFISH, verify runtime evidence in the full text, normalize only comparable measurements, and identify scheduler-safe evidence.

normalization_policy.average_method: Unweighted arithmetic mean of one accepted paper-level mean per independent paper, calculated separately for each identical runtime basis.
rejected_as_completion_time: cumulative runtime without a tool-specific successful denominator
runtime for a modified or derivative implementation when exact-tool identity is required
normalization_policy.scheduler_rule: A paper observation remains unschedulable unless its source scene has a compatible Solidity compiler and LOC profile and retains at least 0.2 normalized support; qualified rows are selected by weighted P90 rather than a cross-paper arithmetic mean.

cross_paper_averages.reason: Only two independent papers report a comparable per-KLoC GPTScan measurement, and neither source supplies a scheduler-compatible compiler scene profile.
The ICSE value assumes the reported complete campaign covered all 388 listed projects; project is not contract and is not a supported scheduler basis.

GPTScan.scheduler_recommendation: Do not invent a per-contract GPTScan value. If evidence rows are later ingested, preserve the two per-KLoC observations under independent source IDs and leave them unschedulable until a compatible compiler/LOC scene profile exists. Do not overwrite either paper row with 21.845 seconds/KLoC.

records.decision_reason: Primary tool paper reports both campaign total and a per-KLoC mean for the exact GPTScan implementation.
records.title: GPTScan: Detecting Logic Vulnerabilities in Smart Contracts by Combining GPT with Program Analysis
records.venue: 46th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE 2024)

tool.name: GPTScan
tool.identity_notes: Exact paper implementation; the underlying dated OpenAI model snapshot is not named.

dataset.name: Top200 + Web3Bugs + DefiHacks
dataset.solidity_profile: No compiler-version distribution. Projects use crytic-compiler default configuration; 17 Top200 projects could not be compiled for static confirmation, but the paper still reports a complete overall scan campaign.

runtime.normalization_formula: 6793.35 seconds / 472.02 KLoC = 14.39 seconds/KLoC (paper-reported); conditional project average = 6793.35 / 388 = 17.508634 seconds/project.
runtime.runtime_denominator_notes: The paper does not tabulate successful executions separately from the 388 project list.

evidence.fact: 303 Top200, 72 Web3Bugs, and 13 DefiHacks projects sum to 388; files and LoC sum to 3,157 and 472,024.
Overall 472.02 KLoC, 6,793.35 seconds, and 14.39 seconds/KLoC; timing covers GPT interaction and static analysis.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6, implementation and dataset setup
evidence.fact: GPT-3.5-turbo is used; 17 Top200 projects cannot be compiled for static confirmation.

scheduler.reason: Per-KLoC is supported, but the source row has no compiler bucket/profile and therefore cannot satisfy scene compatibility and support rules.

records.decision_reason: Independent rerun reports a mean and median over 60 completed per-case observations, but per-case is not a scheduler basis and the GPT model alias had drifted.
records.title: IntentChecker: An Intent-Model-Based Debugging Assistant for Mitigating Numeric Logic Errors in Solidity

tool.name: GPTScan
tool.model: OpenAI model alias reached by the GPTScan implementation during April 2026 reruns
tool.identity_notes: The authors explicitly warn that GPTScan's OpenAI aliases had been redirected since 2023, so this is an exact-code rerun with model drift rather than the original ICSE model snapshot.

dataset.name: 20 RQ1-mitigated numeric-logic-error cases
dataset.canonical_identity: 20 contract/function cases selected from the paper's 75 effective cases; three runs per tool
dataset.solidity_profile: No complete compiler distribution for the 20-case subset. The broader benchmark includes contracts targeting Solidity >=0.6 and one 0.4.x pragma with semantically compatible constructs.

runtime.timeout_policy: No GPTScan timeout is stated; the separate 1,800-second timeout applies to NumScout only.
runtime.hardware: 11th Gen Intel Core i7-11390H at 3.40 GHz, 16 GB RAM, Windows 10 64-bit; same hardware, OS, and network for all compared tools.
runtime.normalization_formula: Use the reported 265.9 seconds/case directly; 60 observations = 20 cases x 3 runs. Do not convert a case into a contract.
runtime.runtime_denominator_notes: Figure 9 contains all 60 per-case observations; an approximate mean-implied total would be 15,954 seconds, but the rounded mean makes that total non-authoritative.

evidence.fact: The common experiment environment is an i7-11390H Windows 10 machine with 16 GB RAM.
GPTScan has n=60, mean 265.9 seconds, and median 149.0 seconds over three runs of 20 cases.
April 2026 reruns used redirected OpenAI aliases; latency used the reruns under common hardware, OS, and network conditions.

scheduler.reason: Per-case is not an accepted scheduler basis; the source also lacks a compiler scene profile and exact model snapshot.

records.decision_reason: Independent deployment reports both project-level and normalized 10-KLoC GPTScan timing; the latter converts cleanly to per-KLoC.

tool.name: GPTScan

dataset.name: D1 + D2 and D3

runtime.runtime_denominator_notes: The paper does not report successful-completion or timeout counts for GPTScan.

records.title: SAILFISH: Vetting Smart Contract State-Inconsistency Bugs in Seconds
records.venue: 2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

tool.name: SAILFISH
tool.identity_notes: Exact paper implementation; no commit hash is printed in the paper.

dataset.name: Etherscan full dataset
dataset.solidity_profile: Contracts requiring Solidity <0.3.x and Vyper contracts were excluded before the 89,853-contract dataset. The paper notes 0.8.3 as the latest compiler at writing but gives no version histogram; errors include unsupported versions and framework/infrastructure failures.

runtime.hardware: Celery 4.4.4 cluster of six Ubuntu 18.04.3 servers; each has Intel Xeon E5-2690 v2 at 3.00 GHz, 40 cores, and 256 GB memory.
runtime.normalization_formula: Use the paper-reported full-dataset mean of 30.79 seconds/contract directly.
runtime.runtime_denominator_notes: Safe + unsafe = 85,247 completed analyses, but Table IV does not explicitly state whether its mean excludes timeout/error cases; do not reconstruct a total from the mean.

evidence.locator: PDF p.10, Section VIII-A and Table II
evidence.fact: Dataset, hardware, 20-minute budget, and outcomes are 83,171 safe, 2,076 unsafe, 1,211 timeout, and 3,395 error.

evidence.locator: PDF p.12, Table IV and Section VIII-C
evidence.fact: SAILFISH mean times are 9.80, 80.78, 246.89, and 30.79 seconds for small, medium, large, and full datasets.

scheduler.reason: Per-contract is supported, but the source has no compiler-bucket distribution/profile to establish scene compatibility.

records.decision_reason: Independent USENIX evaluation reports SAILFISH average time per contract and enough exception counts to reconstruct attempted and completed cases.
records.title: Smart Learning to Find Dumb Contracts

tool.name: SAILFISH
tool.identity_notes: Table 3 identifies the used SAILFISH release by year 2022, but no version or commit is given.

dataset.name: Elysium source subset + Reentrancy benchmark + SolidiFI reentrancy subset
dataset.solidity_profile: No compiler distribution. Sources were lightly cleaned and sometimes moderately upgraded; the authors attribute SAILFISH's 87.8% mean completion rate to an old Slither version incompatible with newer Solidity.

runtime.hardware: 12-core 3.2 GHz Intel Core i7-8700 desktop with 16 GB memory
runtime.normalization_formula: Use Figure 1's reported 10.9 seconds/contract. Completed count derives as (59-6) + (472-125) + (444-0) = 844; do not multiply 10.9 by 844 because Figure 1 does not state a pooled denominator.
runtime.runtime_denominator_notes: The 87.8% completion figure is the unweighted mean of the three test completion rates, while the exact weighting behind the 10.9-second runtime marker is not stated.

evidence.fact: The SAILFISH runtime marker is 10.9 seconds per contract and its mean completion rate is 87.8%.
The test machine is an i7-8700 desktop with 16 GB memory; benchmark sizes and source cleaning are described.
SAILFISH exceptions are 6/59, 125/472, and 0/444 for its three reentrancy tests.

scheduler.reason: Per-contract is supported, but compiler versions, runtime weighting, and exact tool version are insufficient for compatible scene support.

records.decision_reason: Independent FSE evaluation directly reports mean time per analyzed contract and the analyzed count.

tool.name: SAILFISH
tool.identity_notes: Baseline tool is SAILFISH configured for both reentrancy and transaction-ordering attacks; no commit is provided.

dataset.name: D1 Immunefi/Etherscan-network dataset
dataset.canonical_identity: 4,502 contracts from 174 active projects across 11 Etherscan networks
dataset.solidity_profile: No version distribution. The authors state that unsupported Solidity versions prevent SAILFISH from analyzing most contracts; the 3,000 residual non-analyzed cases are not separately classified.

runtime.hardware: x86_64 server with four 24-core 2.10 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8160 CPUs, Debian 9
runtime.normalization_formula: Use the reported 29.34 seconds per analyzed contract directly; mean-implied successful runtime = 29.34 x 1,484 = 43,540.56 seconds, but that derived total is not a paper-reported total.
runtime.runtime_denominator_notes: The surrounding text links the mean to analyzed contracts; Table 1 reports 1,484 analyzed and 18 timeouts.

evidence.fact: D1 has 4,502 contracts; hardware and a 20-minute per-contract timeout are specified.
SAILFISH analyzes 1,484 contracts and has 18 timeouts.
SAILFISH averages 29.34 seconds per analyzed contract and unsupported Solidity versions explain most failures.

scheduler.reason: Per-contract is supported, but the paper supplies no compiler distribution and documents extensive version incompatibility.

records.decision_reason: Runtime is valid empirical evidence but its unit is a vulnerability case/contract group, not an individual contract.

records.venue: 2024 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

tool.name: SAILFISH
tool.identity_notes: SAILFISH baseline; no version is printed. Baselines are run on each member contract and aggregated to a contract-group case.

dataset.name: Front-running vulnerability benchmark
dataset.canonical_identity: 513 real-world vulnerable contract groups, each containing one or more contracts and one exploited vulnerability
dataset.solidity_profile: No version distribution. The authors attribute SAILFISH's 428 errors to unsupported newer Solidity versions.

runtime.timeout_policy: 3 hours per contract-group analysis for each tool; Nyx additionally uses a 15-minute SMT timeout per function pair.
runtime.hardware: AMD Ryzen 3975X, 512 GB RAM, single-thread execution
runtime.normalization_formula: Use 32.83 seconds per successfully analyzed group/case only. Mean-implied total = 32.83 x 84 = 2,757.72 seconds; do not divide by member contracts because group cardinalities are not reported per case.
runtime.runtime_denominator_notes: Table 1 labels 84 cases as successfully analyzed and time as average analysis time; groups may contain multiple contracts.

evidence.locator: PDF p.9, benchmark and experiment settings
evidence.fact: The benchmark has 513 one-or-more-contract groups; baseline tools analyze member contracts individually, then aggregate results.
SAILFISH has 1 timeout, 428 errors, 84 successfully analyzed groups, 1,260.87 average LoC, and 32.83-second average time.

scheduler.reason: Contract-group/case is not per-contract, and the source lacks a compiler profile.

records.decision_reason: The paper reports 1 minute 40 seconds cumulative SAILFISH time over a 49-contract dataset but not SAILFISH's successful completion count.
